articles.body:

It follows disorder last month when students began protesting over school conditions.

The protests became broader and represented other concerns some French people have about issues in the country.

French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu announced on Monday that local authorities would be able to implement a partial curfew to protect people and businesses.

articles.title: Carol Peixinho celebra 1 ano e 1 mês do filho com Tiaguinho | G1
articles.standfirst: Bento completou o primeiro ano de vida no dia 19 de outubro. Em homenagem compartilhada nesta segunda-feira (19), mãe coruja disse que ganhou na loteria.
articles.summary: Bento completou o primeiro ano de vida no dia 19 de outubro. Em homenagem compartilhada nesta segunda-feira (19), mãe coruja disse que ganhou na loteria
articles.body:
Carol Peixinho mantém clima de 'mêsversário' e celebra 1 ano e 1 mês do filho com Thiaguinho — Foto: Redes Sociais

A influenciadora digital Carol Peixinho manteve o clima de "mêsversário" e usou as redes sociais, nesta segunda-feira (19), para celebrar a marca de 1 ano e 1 mês do filho com o cantor Tiaguinho, o pequeno Bento.

Além de compartilhar uma mensagem carinhosa, onde afirmava ter ganhado na loteria quando descobriu estar grávida, a baiana também mostrou para os fãs uma foto fofa da família. Na legenda aproveitou para se declarar.

"1 ano e 1 mês do nosso grande amor", escreveu.

Bento completou 1 ano no dia 19 de setembro . Na ocasião, Carol Peixinho e Thiaguinho marcaram a data por meio de vídeos e fotos publicados no Instagram.

Logo nas primeiras horas do dia do aniversário de Bento, a influenciadora digital publicou um vídeo brincando e cantando com o filho, afirmando estar na espera do pai para celebrar, já que o cantor havia feito um show em outro estado na noite anterior.

Ela também compartilhou uma coletânea de momentos ao lado do filho desde o nascimento. Com um texto cheio de orgulho, a influenciadora citou uma experiência de renascimento após dar à luz ao filho, destacando a travessia entre momentos difíceis e preciosos.

"Eu viveria tudinho novamente. Não tiraria nada desse nosso primeiro capítulo.Sou profundamente grata a Deus por ter me escolhido para ser sua mãezinha", disse.

Peixinho ainda compartilhou um registro de um pequinique feito especialmente para Bento. Na imagem, é possível ver uma toalha quadriculada azul, coberta com balões e brinquedos de pelúcia.

Carol Peixinho e Thiaguinho celebram aniversário de 1 ano do filho — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

O pequeno também ganhou homenagem do pai, no palco do show que o cantor fez em Minas Gerais. Na virada do dia, ele pediu ajuda da plateia, com direito a palmas e música de parabéns.

Mais tarde, ele publicou um carrossel de fotos com registros de momentos com Bento, acompanhado de uma homenagem emocionada e cheia de gratidão para o filho.

"Eu achava que conhecia o amor. Mas não sabia que era possível amar alguém mais do que a mim mesmo. Há 1 ano eu acordo e penso primeiro em você, depois em mim. Seu sorriso me dá forças quando estou cansado. Quando você segura minha mão, me sinto o cara mais forte do mundo", escreveu.

No texto, ele afirmou ainda que a chegada de Bento mudou a vida do casal, além de agradecer ao pequeno. "Você encheu nossa casa e vida de LUZ. Eu já nem consigo me lembrar de como era a vida sem você e sem esse amor que transborda o meu coração", afirmou.

articles.title: Protestos na França: vídeo mostra saque e invasão de loja em Nice | G1
articles.standfirst: Grupo entrou no local destruindo vitrines e produtos, com sacolas para levar o que conseguisse roubar.
articles.summary: Protestos na França contra o custo de vida resultam em saques em Nice, confrontos violentos e quase 1.800 detidos em todo o país.
articles.body:
Câmeras de segurança registraram o momento em que uma loja de acessórios para celular foi atacada em Nice, na França, durante as manifestações que ocorreram em todo o país no sábado (17).

A invasão começou com um grupo menor, que entrou destruindo vitrines e produtos, com vários segurando sacolas para saquear o local nas mãos.

Jovens roubam produtos de loja em Nice após invasão — Foto: PHONE CASE NICE via REUTERS

Após a entrada deles, vários outros invadiram o local também e começaram a pegar todos os produtos que podiam.

Essa foi um dos muitos saques a lojas em Nice e outras cidades francesas. O sábado de protestos, que tiveram muito tumulto e violência, terminou com um morto, mais de 500 policiais feridos e quase 1.800 detidos.

Segundo o Ministério do Interior, mais de 500 mil pessoas foram às ruas em dezenas de cidades. Os atos marcam a união de um movimento estudantil que já dura um mês com a insatisfação geral da população contra o aumento do custo de vida.

Embora centenas de milhares de pessoas tenham protestado pacificamente, grupos radicais entraram em confronto com as forças de segurança.

Grupo invadindo loja de acessórios de celular em Nice — Foto: REUTERS

articles.title: Pai e filho ficam ilhados em rio após barco ser levado pela correnteza | G1
articles.standfirst: Homem de 46 anos e o filho dele, de 15, estavam montando o acampamento em uma ilha, no Rio Paranaíba, em Araguari, quando o barco foi levado pela correnteza. Ambos foram resgatados pelo Corpo de Bombeiros.
articles.summary: Homem de 46 anos e o filho dele, de 15, estavam montando o acampamento em uma ilha, no Rio Paranaíba, em Araguari, quando o barco foi levado pela correnteza.
articles.body:
Um homem de 46 anos e o filho dele, de 15, ficaram ilhados no Rio Paranaíba, em Araguari , no Triângulo Mineiro, na madrugada de domingo (18). Segundo o Corpo de Bombeiros, que realizou o resgate, o pai e o filho estavam montando um acampamento quando o barco deles foi levado pela correnteza.

Um vídeo gravado pelos bombeiros mostra o momento do resgate. Nas imagens, os militares se deslocam pelo rio até chegar ao pai e o filho, que aparecem no escuro esperando na ilha. Veja o vídeo acima.

Com a correnteza, o barco ficou à deriva e, com isso, a dupla perdeu vários pertences que estavam na embarcação.

Os bombeiros acessaram o rio por um ponto situado a 15 quilômetros, por via fluvial, da ilha na qual as vítimas estavam. O pai e o filho foram resgatados sem ferimentos e levados à casa da família deles em Araguari.

O Corpo de Bombeiros reforçou que, antes de atividades em rio e represas, é fundamental amarrar e ancorar bem a embarcação. Além disso, também é importante avisar alguém de confiança sobre o local e horário previsto de retorno.

Bombeiros resgataram os dois e os levaram até a casa deles em Araguari — Foto: Corpo de Bombeiros/Divulgação

Pai e filho estavam montando acampamento quando correnteza levou o barco — Foto: Corpo de Bombeiros/Divulgação

articles.title: Justiça dos EUA emite ordem de prisão a Raúl Castro | G1
articles.standfirst: Ex-presidente de Cuba foi acusado de homicídio em derrubada de avião de grupo que tentava resgatar cubanos, em 1996. Na ocasião, ele era ministro de seu irmão, Raúl Castro. Ordem de prisão ocorre em meio a temores de invasão dos EUA à ilha.
articles.summary: A Justiça dos Estados Unidos emitiu nesta segunda-feira (19) uma ordem de prisão contra o ex-presidente cubano Raúl Castro, ex-presidente de Cuba e irmão de Fidel Castro.
articles.body:
Raúl Castro em 1º de maio de 2025 em Havana, Cuba — Foto: Norlys Perez / Reuters

A Justiça dos Estados Unidos emitiu nesta segunda-feira (19) uma ordem de prisão contra o ex-presidente cubano Raúl Castro , segundo anunciou o procurador-geral do estado da Flórida, James Uthmeyer.

➡️ A ordem de prisão é parte do processo que corria na Justiça da Flórida contra Castro por homicídio . O ex-presidente cubano, de 94 anos, também responde por dois crimes de destruição de aeronave e um crime de conspiração para matar cidadãos dos EUA, todos relativos a um episódio de fevereiro de 1996, quando Raúl era ministro da Defesa de seu irmão, Fidel Castro ( leia mais abaixo ).

"Raúl Castro ordenou o assassinato premeditado, sancionado pelo Estado, de quatro moradores da Flórida, a sangue-frio. A Flórida jamais deixará de buscar a responsabilização pelos casos de Carlos Costa, Pablo Morales, Mario de la Peña e Armando Alejandre Jr.", disse o procurador-geral.

A ordem foi emitida por um tribunal de Miami, segundo Uthmeyer. O regime cubano — atualmente comandado por Miguel Díaz-Canel, aliado dos irmãos Castro — ainda não havia se pronunciado sobre o anúncio até a última atualização desta reportagem.

👉 A ordem de prisão também ocorre em um momento em que os Estados Unidos vêm pressionando Cuba para uma mudança de regime . Os dois países vêm travando negociações discretas, em meio a temores de uma invasão de forças norte-americanas à ilha , que vem sofrendo fortes apagões por conta do colapso da economia.

PENA DE MORTE E PRISÃO PERPÉTUA: veja a quais penas Raúl Castro estaria sujeito

Os processos aos que Raúl Castro responde na Justiça norte-americana são relativos a um incidente ocorrido há 30 anos: a derrubada de dois aviões civis em fevereiro de 1996.

O caso é considerado um dos episódios mais delicados da relação entre EUA e Cuba e ocorreu quando Raúl Castro era ministro da Defesa. A ilha estava então sob o comando de seu irmão, Fidel Castro (1926-2016).

As aeronaves pertenciam ao grupo Brothers to the Rescue (“Irmãos ao Resgate”), formado por cubanos anticastristas exilados nos EUA. Os quatro tripulantes morreram, três deles cidadãos americanos.

articles.title: Baixa umidade na Paraíba: Inmet emite alerta para 101 cidades | G1
articles.standfirst: Período de aviso começou na manhã desta segunda-feira (19) e segue até o fim do dia. Durante o alerta, a umidade relativa do ar pode chegar a 20% nas cidades.
articles.summary: Com índices de até 20%, o alerta de baixa umidade na Paraíba atinge 101 cidades nesta segunda-feira (19) e exige cuidados redobrados com a saúde.
articles.body:
O Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia (Inmet) emitiu, nesta segunda-feira (19), um alerta amarelo de baixa umidade do ar para 101 municípios da Paraíba . O período de aviso começou na manhã desta segunda-feira (19) e segue até o fim do dia. Veja lista de municípios afetados abaixo.

Durante o período do alerta, a umidade relativa do ar deve variar entre 30% e 20% , índices considerados abaixo do recomendado para a saúde.

Segundo o Inmet, há baixo risco de incêndios florestais e de impactos à saúde, mas a população deve adotar medidas de prevenção para reduzir os efeitos do tempo seco.

evite atividades físicas intensas nos horários mais quentes;

procure permanecer em locais protegidos do sol entre o fim da manhã e a tarde.

Em caso de emergência, a população pode acionar a Defesa Civil, pelo telefone 199, ou o Corpo de Bombeiros, pelo telefone 193.

articles.title: Previsão do tempo para Uberlândia e região: calor de 37 °C e chuva | G1
articles.standfirst: Temperaturas devem ficar de 1°C a 3°C acima da média do período entre os dias 19 e 25 de outubro. Chuvas isoladas estão previstas para o Triângulo Mineiro e Alto Paranaíba.
articles.summary: A previsão do tempo para Uberlândia e região indica calor de até 37 °C e pancadas de chuva isoladas sob influência de sistema de alta pressão no Atlântico.
articles.body:
Temperaturas mais elevadas devem ser sentidas em momentos com menor cobertura de nuvens — Foto: Adreana Oliveira/g1

A semana será de calor e possibilidade possibilidade de tempestades no Triângulo Mineiro e Alto Paranaíba entre essa segunda-feira (19) e domingo (25). As temperaturas tendem a estar de 1°C a 3°C acima do padrão esperado para o período e com máximas que podem atingir até 37 °C em algumas regiões. As chuvas devem ficar abaixo da média em parte das duas regiões, com precipitações entre 10 e 20 mm.

"As temperaturas mais elevadas podem ser percebidas principalmente nos períodos de maior incidência de sol e menor cobertura de nuvens", afirma o geógrafo William Borges.

De acordo com Borges, esse cenário é percebido por causa da influência da Alta Subtropical do Atlântico Sul (ASAS).

🔎ASAS: É um dos grandes sistemas de alta pressão permanentes da circulação geral da atmosfera, que se movimenta sobre o oceano Atlântico Sul, entre o Brasil, onde influencia o tempo, especialmente no Sudeste e Nordeste do país. Ele traz menos nuvens e chuva, mais horas de sol forte e dias mais quentes.

William Borges destaca ainda que, apesar das temperaturas acima da média climatológica, não são descartadas as possibilidades de pancadas de chuvas sobre o Triângulo Mineiro e Alto Paranaíba entre essa quarta-feira (21) e quinta-feira (22). Essas precipitações tendem a ocorrer especialmente durante as tardes e noites, período em que o aquecimento e a disponibilidade de umidade podem favorecer a formação de instabilidades.

As maiores máximas são da cidade de Ituiutaba , com até 37 °C, e Araguari , com 36 °C. Já as menores ficam em Araxá , com mínima de 14 °C, e Uberlândia apresenta mínimas de até 15 °C e máximas de até 35 °C.

*Estagiário sob supervisão de Adreana Oliveira

articles.title: Bracell fortalece agenda de inclusão para pessoas com deficiência | G1
articles.standfirst: Iniciativas reúnem atração de talentos, capacitação de colaboradores, diálogo com a sociedade e ações para ampliar oportunidades e pertencimento.
articles.summary: Iniciativas reúnem atração de talentos, capacitação de colaboradores, diálogo com a sociedade e ações para ampliar oportunidades e pertencimento.
articles.body:
Colaboradoras da área de Recursos Humanos da Bracell conduzem oficina de carreira para pessoas com deficiência na Casa Bracell Social, durante a programação da Semana Pertencer — Foto: Acervo Bracell

Criar oportunidades, eliminar barreiras e construir um ambiente em que as pessoas possam desenvolver seus talentos . É a partir dessa perspectiva que empresas vêm fortalecendo sua atuação voltada à inclusão de pessoas com deficiência, por meio de iniciativas de atração de profissionais, sensibilização de colaboradores e diálogo com a sociedade.

Na Bracell , essa agenda faz parte da estratégia de Diversidade e Inclusão e está conectada ao Bracell 2030 , estratégia de sustentabilidade de longo prazo da companhia. No pilar Empoderando Vidas, um dos compromissos é promover um ambiente de trabalho cada vez mais inclusivo.

Na prática, esse compromisso se traduz em diferentes frentes: da busca por profissionais que são pessoas com deficiência à capacitação de colaboradores e participação em espaços de diálogo com a sociedade. Também aparece em atitudes que nascem no próprio ambiente de trabalho e ajudam a transformar relações.

Foi assim com Eliana Aparecida dos Santos , colaboradora da Bracell há sete anos. No viveiro de Lençóis Paulista, onde atualmente atua na área de irrigação, ela conheceu um colega com deficiência auditiva e passou a perceber os desafios que ele enfrentava no dia a dia.

Eliana Aparecida dos Santos, aprendeu Libras para se comunicar com um colega com deficiência auditiva e transformou a iniciativa em uma forma de contribuir para a inclusão no ambiente de trabalho — Foto: Acervo pessoal

Eliana já tinha vontade de aprender Língua Brasileira de Sinais (Libras) , mas a convivência com o colega transformou o interesse em ação. Começou sozinha, aprendendo o alfabeto e os números, e depois buscou formação em Libras em Lençóis Paulista. “ Foi por amor que aprendi, por amor à pessoa com deficiência auditiva. A primeira palavra que eu aprendi foi ‘obrigada’. Eu nunca vou esquecer disso ”, relata.

A primeira comunicação em Libras foi marcante para os dois. “ Ele ficou muito feliz e me incentivou a continuar. Até hoje eu aprendo muito com ele ”, conta.

A iniciativa foi reconhecida dentro da companhia e abriu espaço para que Eliana também contribuísse com Libras em atividades relacionadas à inclusão. Para ela, incluir significa permitir que as pessoas mostrem seus talentos. “ Muitas pessoas têm formação, mas acabam ficando invisíveis. Então você dar essa chance a elas, isso é incluir. Fazer o outro se sentir parte do processo ”, afirma.

Além das ações de conscientização, a Bracell mantém uma atuação voltada à atração de profissionais que são pessoa com deficiência. Um comitê interno, formado por colaboradores e profissionais de Recursos Humanos, acompanha o tema e busca identificar talentos e oportunidades dentro da companhia.

Todas as vagas abertas pela empresa estão disponíveis para candidatura de pessoas com deficiência, por meio do portal bracell.com/carreiras , onde os profissionais também podem cadastrar seus currículos. Além disso, a companhia mantém vagas afirmativas destinadas exclusivamente a esse público.

Para Priscilla Reuter , gerente de Desenvolvimento de Recursos Humanos da Bracell em São Paulo, ampliar a inclusão passa tanto pela criação de oportunidades quanto pela preparação do ambiente de trabalho.

“A inclusão precisa estar presente nas oportunidades, mas também nas relações e na forma como as pessoas convivem no dia a dia. Por isso, trabalhamos em diferentes frentes, desde a atração de profissionais até a sensibilização e capacitação das nossas equipes”, afirma.

Participante da oficina de carreira para pessoas com deficiência realizada na Casa Bracell Social durante a Semana Pertencer — Foto: Acervo Bracell

Uma das iniciativas que integram essa atuação é a Semana Pertencer, realizada pela Bracell em agosto deste ano com o conceito “Conhecer, Sensibilizar e Conectar” . A programação reuniu ações voltadas à diversidade, inclusão, empregabilidade e pertencimento.

O trabalho de sensibilização foi estruturado para alcançar diferentes níveis da organização.

“Começamos capacitando a diretoria, depois as gerências, avançamos para coordenadores e equipes administrativas e chegamos também aos colaboradores das áreas mais operacionais. A ideia é que esse processo de engajamento seja sistêmico e que a inclusão aconteça de forma respeitosa em todos os níveis da companhia”, explica Priscilla.

Em uma das etapas, aproximadamente 140 colaboradores participaram de capacitações presenciais sobre inclusão na prática, envolvendo trainees, profissionais da manutenção automotiva e colaboradores do viveiro.

A atuação da Bracell também se estende ao diálogo com o poder público e a sociedade. Em Lençóis Paulista, a companhia integra o Conselho Municipal de Pessoas com Deficiência , que atua na articulação de políticas públicas e iniciativas relacionadas à promoção dos direitos desse público. O gerente de Auditoria Interna da Bracell, Nelson Freitas de Abreu , ocupa a vice-presidência do Conselho, tendo Priscilla Reuter como suplente.

O Conselho também participou do encerramento da Semana Pertencer na Bracell , ampliando o diálogo sobre direitos, inclusão, empregabilidade e o papel das empresas e da sociedade na construção de ambientes mais inclusivos.

Colaboradores da Bracell em agenda da Semana Pertencer, no Bracell Learning Institute, em Lençóis Paulista (SP) — Foto: Acervo Bracell

A Semana Pertencer integra o Programa Pertencer , iniciativa estruturante da Bracell voltada à inclusão de pessoas com deficiência. O programa tem como propósito fortalecer uma cultura de pertencimento, promovendo condições para que os profissionais ingressem, se desenvolvam e construam suas trajetórias na companhia.

“Baseado em princípios como respeito às singularidades, acessibilidade e equidade de oportunidades, o Programa Pertencer atua de forma transversal, conectando diferentes áreas da empresa para promover ambientes mais inclusivos e acolhedores. A iniciativa é apoiada por uma governança dedicada, formada por lideranças, Recursos Humanos e um comitê interno responsável por acompanhar indicadores e impulsionar ações voltadas ao avanço contínuo da inclusão na Bracell”, detalha Priscilla Reuter.

Equipe do Viveiro da Bracell, em Lençóis Paulista (SP), durante atividade da Semana Pertencer, que reuniu ações de sensibilização e conscientização sobre diversidade e inclusão — Foto: Acervo Bracell

A Bracell é uma das líderes globais na produção de celulose solúvel e especial, com expertise no cultivo sustentável de eucalipto, base para a fabricação de celulose de alta qualidade. Com operações no Brasil desde 2003, a empresa integra o grupo Royal Golden Eagle (RGE), com sede em Singapura. Conta com mais de 11 mil colaboradores e duas unidades industriais no país — em Camaçari (BA) e Lençóis Paulista (SP) — além de escritório administrativo em Singapura e estruturas comerciais na Ásia, Europa e Estados Unidos. articles.title: Mulher é picada por cobra, consegue capturá-la e a leva a hospital | G1
articles.standfirst: Mulher foi atacada em fazenda de Montividiu ao recolher folhas secas. Médica alerta que transportar réptil gera perigo de novo ataque e recomenda apenas fotos à distância.
articles.summary: Mulher foi atacada em fazenda de Montividiu ao recolher folhas secas. Médica alerta que transportar réptil gera perigo de novo ataque e recomenda apenas fotos à distância.
articles.body:
Uma mulher foi picada por uma cobra após fazer a limpeza do quintal de uma fazenda em Montividiu , no sudoeste de Goiás. Ela levou o animal até uma Unidade de Pronto Atendimento (UPA) para que a equipe de saúde identificasse a espécie e aplicasse o antídoto (assista acima) . Ao g1 , a médica Luana Borboleta afirmou que transportar animal pode gerar um novo ataque .

"O principal risco aí é de acontecer um outro acidente. Como leigo, pode ser difícil a identificação do óbito de um réptil e, num momento oportuno, ela deferir um novo ataque", disse Luana.

O acidente ocorreu quando a mulher retornou a um monte de folhas secas que havia juntado. O nome da mulher não foi divulgado. Segundo a reportagem da TV Anhanguera, ao pegar as folhas, ela não viu que a serpente estava enrolada sob a folhagem e foi atingida por dois botes, que acertaram dois dedos de uma das mãos.

Já morta, a mulher decidiu transportar a cobra até o pronto atendimento. No local, os profissionais do plantão reconheceram o animal como sendo uma jararacuçu, agilizando a escolha do soro antiofídico adequado. A paciente permaneceu internada em observação clínica, apresentou evolução estável e teve previsão de alta médica confirmada para esta segunda-feira (19).

Mulher é picada por cobra, consegue capturá-la e a leva a hospital — Foto: Reprodução/TV Anhanguera

Luana orientou que a remoção do réptil do local do acidente é totalmente desnecessária para salvar a vítima. O procedimento seguro consiste em manter distância e fazer fotos do corpo inteiro do animal utilizando o zoom da câmera do celular, levando apenas as imagens para visualização médica no pronto-socorro.

Luana explicou ainda que, em Goiás, os acidentes mais comuns com viperídeos envolvem cascavéis. Segundo ela, identificar a espécie exata não altera a conduta hospitalar, pois o soro antibotrópico disponível na rede pública é formulado a partir de um conjunto das principais espécies do gênero, garantindo a neutralização eficaz da peçonha.

articles.title: Polícia de Israel prende 10 suspeitos por ataques a jornalista | G1
articles.standfirst: Agressões ocorreram no fim de semana e provocaram cobranças dos Estados Unidos, da França, da Bélgica e da Polônia por medidas contra a violência de colonos israelenses.
articles.summary: Agressões ocorreram no fim de semana e provocaram cobranças dos Estados Unidos, da França, da Bélgica e da Polônia por medidas contra a violência de colonos israelenses.
articles.body:
A polícia de Israel informou nesta segunda-feira (19) que prendeu dez suspeitos em uma investigação sobre episódios de violência registrados no fim de semana na Cisjordânia ocupada. Entre os casos estão ataques contra a fotojornalista do jornal "The Washington Post", Heidi Levine, e diplomatas europeus .

Os Estados Unidos , principal aliado de Israel , cobraram medidas para conter a violência de colonos israelenses e prender os responsáveis pela agressão à jornalista. França, Bélgica e Polônia também exigiram providências após o ataque a seus diplomatas.

Segundo a polícia, os suspeitos foram detidos em uma operação realizada antes do amanhecer. Eles são investigados por envolvimento em atos de violência, desrespeito a uma ordem que restringia o acesso a uma zona militar e construção ilegal.

Os nomes dos detidos não foram divulgados. Eles foram levados para interrogatório, segundo a polícia. A Rádio do Exército de Israel informou que todos são cidadãos israelenses.

Processos judiciais contra colonos israelenses são raros.

Colonos israelenses vestidos de preto e mascarados queimam oliveiras em ataque na Cisjordânia — Foto: REUTERS/Ammar Awad

O embaixador dos Estados Unidos em Israel , Mike Huckabee, afirmou na rede social X que as prisões representavam um “desdobramento muito positivo” na busca e punição dos responsáveis por atacar e espancar a jornalista Heidi Levine.

Na última sexta-feira (19), colonos israelenses mascarados foram filmados agredindo Levine, cidadã americana que acompanhava a colheita de azeitonas por palestinos na Cisjordânia . Ela foi levada ao hospital e passou por uma cirurgia em um dedo.

No sábado (17), diplomatas da França, da Bélgica e da Polônia , além de um prefeito francês, foram atacados por colonos mascarados em outra área da Cisjordânia . Um veículo diplomático belga também foi danificado.

O ministro das Relações Exteriores de Israel , Gideon Saar, e as Forças Armadas atribuíram o ataque aos diplomatas a “manifestantes israelenses”.

O primeiro-ministro Benjamin Netanyahu, por sua vez, adotou um tom mais cauteloso. Sua coalizão nacionalista e religiosa enfrenta as eleições de 27 de outubro sob a perspectiva de perder a maioria no governo.

Netanyahu afirmou que os diplomatas entraram em uma “área sensível com histórico de confrontos” sem coordenar a visita com as Forças Armadas. Sobre a agressão a Levine, disse que as circunstâncias ainda eram “pouco claras”.

articles.title: Volunteers help save one of London's rarest plants
articles.summary: Tower mustard has suffered steep decline in London but has been successfully grown and replanted.
articles.body:
More than 1,000 tower mustard plants have been successfully grown and planted out by volunteers in London.

It marks a successful first year for a major community-led effort to restore one of the capital's rarest native wildflowers, vital for bees, butterflies and rare moths.

Led by Citizen Zoo and Habitats & Heritage, the tower mustard project brings together a network of land managers, community groups, conservation partners and volunteers.

The plants, grown by volunteers, are being reestablished at sites across London, in regions where tower mustard was previously known to occur.

At the core of the project are the Mighty Mustard volunteers.

In March, they attended a workshop, learned how to sow the tiny seeds, and were given their own growing equipment, including pots, seed trays and soil.

Seeds were sourced from London's last remaining tower mustard populations in Lesnes Abbey Woods in Bexley and Stain Hill Reservoir in Richmond-upon-Thames.

Charlotte Harris, nature conservation manager at Habitats & Heritage, said: "[We] are passionate about engaging people in conservation initiatives. Through this tower mustard project, we have enjoyed giving local residents the unique opportunity to get hands-on in conserving one of London's rarest plants.

"We've found the volunteers have become really attached to [them]."

Seeds have now been planted at Wimbledon Common, Hounslow Heath, Lesnes Abbey Woods and Barnes Common.

Harris added: "We are hoping that this model can be used as a blueprint for helping other rare plants with volunteer input in the same way."

The final planting day is at Hampton Court Palace's Home Park on Tuesday, where plants raised separately by the Historic Royal Palaces Gardens Team and volunteers will be used.

Botanist Dr Mark Spencer has also provided expert support throughout the project.

Tower mustard, or Turritis glabra, is a native UK herb that has suffered steep decline due to habitat destruction and changes in land management.

It is thought to survive at around 30 sites across England.

The species is assessed as near threatened on the Great Britain Red List and endangered in England.

Growing to around one metre tall and producing delicate white flowers, tower mustard is associated with open and disturbed habitats and supports pollinators.

This community-led model builds on Citizen Zoo's successful Hop of Hope project which saw volunteers rear large marsh grasshoppers from eggs at home, going on to release the species in wetlands across Norfolk.

Elliot Newton, director of rewilding at Citizen Zoo, said the company hopes to roll out more projects to preserve plants in the face of climate change.

"In London alone, we've lost 185 species of plant. They have gone extinct in recent history."

He said Citizen Zoo have many other plants on their radar, including copse bindweed, a native British climbing plant.

Tower mustard is the first plant species Citizen Zoo has worked with in London, joining a growing portfolio of rewilding projects that also includes beavers, water voles, German hairy snails and white storks.

The tower mustard project is funded by the Greater London Authority's Green Roots Fund and Thames Water.

The project brings together Habitats & Heritage, Barnes Common, Lesnes Abbey Woods, Wimbledon Common, London Borough of Hounslow, London Borough of Richmond upon Thames and Historic Royal Palaces.

Newton said: "These projects may sound small, but they're helping safeguard the future of the city."

articles.title: Russia’s Lavrov discusses US war and regional security during Tehran visit
articles.summary: GCC states have pressed Moscow to help halt Iranian attacks and reopen the Strait of Hormuz.
articles.body:
Tehran, Iran – Russia’s Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov has met his Iranian counterpart Abbas Araghchi in Tehran, to discuss the war with the United States and efforts to end it.

Lavrov landed in the Iranian capital on Monday afternoon on his first visit to Iran since February 2025. Araghchi said talks with Lavrov had focused on regional developments, including the US-Israeli war on Iran.

He also called out Israel’s “dangerous expansion” in the region, which he blamed for the current hostilities.

“The existing insecurity around the Strait of Hormuz is a direct result of the military aggression by the US and [Israel] against Iran, and it is ongoing in different forms,” he said.

He added that Iran’s policy was to focus on diplomacy, as regional problems have “no military solution”.

“I believe Europe must also open its eyes to some truths,” Araghchi said. “Just like the Americans, the Europeans suffer from miscalculations and wrong interpretations, and have caused many wars and troubles around the world with their wrong policies.”

Meanwhile, Lavrov said Russia is committed to a 20-year strategic partnership agreement with Iran, which officially came into force on October 2. He said Russian specialists would gradually return to the Bushehr nuclear power plant after they left during the war.

The Russian foreign minister also linked restored navigation with protection for Iran against renewed attacks.

Lavrov held a meeting with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian later on Monday. Pezeshkian said that he believes Russia shared “common views and approaches with Iran” when it came to his call for a world based on mutual respect.

Moscow said Lavrov’s trip was part of efforts to ease months of tension, since the US and Israel launched their war on Iran on February 28.

On Sunday, Lavrov was in Bahrain, which was heavily targeted by Iran during the war, to participate in a strategic dialogue session between Russia and the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC).

He was urged by GCC members to use Moscow’s influence with Tehran to press for “serious dialogue” and restore shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, which has been severely disrupted by attacks on commercial vessels.

GCC chief Jasem Al-Budaiwi said member states had faced more than 7,000 Iranian missiles and drones since the start of the war.

In the council’s closing statement, the six Arab countries said they wanted Iran’s nuclear and missile programmes, as well as its support for regional armed groups, to be included in future talks to end the war.

Nikita Smagin, an analyst and researcher on Iran and Russia’s role in the Middle East, said Lavrov’s trip reflects Moscow’s efforts to maintain working relations with all countries in the region.

He said Lavrov also wants to maintain Russia’s status as a mediator, despite the impact of the Ukraine war on its global reputation.

“The timing of visits to the Gulf monarchies and Iran, taking place almost simultaneously, is a deliberate signal: Moscow wants to show that it approaches relations with all these countries on broadly equal terms and is equally interested in cooperation with each of them,” Smagin said.

Lavrov told GCC ministers in Manama that the region was once again teetering on the brink of a full-scale war and Russia wanted to establish a regional architecture for “collective security”.

He said this could include combining initiatives from countries in the region, along with those put forward by Russia and China, with the aim of restoring maritime traffic and achieving lasting peace. The Russian foreign minister urged other regional states such as Iraq and Jordan, which have also been hit by Iranian strikes, to participate.

Lavrov expressed support for the Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) signed between Iran and the US in June, which later collapsed, as a framework for reducing tension.

Iran has said it wants a return to that agreement, and for Washington to honour a finalised bilateral deal between Iran and Oman to manage territorial waters in the Strait of Hormuz. This has been opposed by the US, which has established its own route in the waterway for shipping.

Intelligence reports cited by US media said that Russia and China are providing military support to Iran in the form of satellite imagery for targeting purposes and components for weapons.

But US President Donald Trump contradicted those reports last week, saying Moscow and Beijing would have “too much to lose” if they helped Iran.

Washington has also issued sanctions waivers for Russia in a bid to lower fuel prices driven up by the war against Iran.

Russia’s position on the Iran war is somewhat unusual, said Smagin. It has a partial interest in the conflict continuing, as higher oil prices and the severe restrictions on Iranian oil reaching China all benefit Moscow.

“Russia and Iran have been competing primarily for the Chinese market, so China is now effectively forced to buy Russian oil at higher prices because Iranian supplies are largely unavailable,” he said.

Smagin added that Russia does not want the conflict to escalate further, as the consequences could be unpredictable, but its leverage over either Iran or the US to influence the course of the conflict remains limited.

Russia will continue to expand relations with Tehran, Smagin said, including through Caspian Sea trade, and limited military cooperation with Iran.

“These efforts appear to be aimed less at generating economic returns than at expanding Russia’s political influence over Iran and the course of events,” he said.

Military strikes by Iran and the US to wrest control of the waterway have continued, with the US midterm elections approaching on November 3 .

In comments to the media, Trump threatened to “soon finish the job” with Iran, to which Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi replied: “We have unfinished jobs too.”

articles.title: French protest violence: A ‘Christmas present’ for Le Pen’s far right?
articles.summary: Le Pen is positioning her party as more capable than centrist or left-wing forces before the 2027 presidential election.
articles.body:
As massive protests swept through cities across France over the weekend, degenerating into riots in many places, far-right politician Marine Le Pen has attempted to profit from the crisis ahead of the presidential election in April 2027.

On Sunday, the leader of the National Rally party, or RN by its French initials, railed against President Emmanuel Macron’s handling of the crisis in a video statement, saying the outgoing centre-right leader no longer has any “credibility or authority” and that the country’s people were caught between his austerity “hammering” them on the one hand and “insurrectionary activists” on the left on the other.

School protests in France erupted on September 21 in a poor borough of Paris as pupils demonstrated against dilapidated infrastructure, teacher shortages and tight class schedules. The demonstrations quickly spread across the country and coincided with a nationwide public sector strike against the government’s plans to cut public spending.

Le Pen blamed the political left and “decades of immigration” to France for the looting and destruction that trailed the demonstrations, and presented her party as capable of restoring order — without offering any firm evidence to back up assertions that the rioting was led by immigrants.

The politician is already far ahead in recent polls, and some say she is likely to be the next leader. Here’s what we know:

Scenes of burned cars, vandalised and looted shops and defaced public buildings emerged from across France.

Some 550,000 people demonstrated on Saturday, according to the Ministry of the Interior, although protest organisers put the figure at 800,000. Protesters included students, union groups and supporters of the “yellow vests” movement, which protested against inflation back in 2018, at the start of Macron’s presidency.

Although most marched peacefully, masked groups attacked city halls in several cities on Saturday, including the 19th-century City Hall in the city of Limoges, which was badly damaged.

In Lyon, a tourist office was set ablaze.

In Marseille, hooded individuals attacked a police station. The city has since banned protests.

Looters also targeted hundreds of shops in several locations.

In Paris, storefronts were shattered and broken glass littered the Place de la Republique. The Marianne statue, an important symbol of France, was partially dismantled. Paris police said one person died of a heart attack, but did not provide more details.

Protesters and rights groups have accused police of using disproportionate force throughout the protests. Some 2,400 people were arrested by Sunday, officials said. Several police officers were injured.

In a national address, Macron condemned rioters and accused far-left groups of attacking police and public buildings. Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said on Monday that partial curfews would be imposed in some areas.

Peter McPhee, a professor emeritus at the University of Melbourne, described the protests as a “Christmas present” for Le Pen’s National Rally ahead of the presidential election.

Le Pen said in a video statement protesters have “legitimate social grievances” but that Macron’s government was “exhausted, disoriented and seemingly incapable” of addressing them.

She criticised the administration’s controversial budget plans and promised to free the French from “Macronist toxic policies” while failing to mention that her party has also proposed strict spending cuts to bring down rising public debt.

The politician, who is far ahead of other candidates in the polls, fuelled right-wing narratives spreading online that immigrants, not the French people, are instigating the protests, even as the grievances driving the agitation have intersected, with flag-carrying pro-Palestinian, environmental, feminist and anticolonial movements joining in.

McPhee called Le Pen’s move “profoundly worrying”.

“It is easy for Le Pen to make the link between the violent attacks on buildings and shops with African migrants because of the Palestinian and Algerian flags,” the professor said. “People in many parts of the world are attracted to simplistic, often racist, answers to economic and social problems.”

Analysts add that far-left leader Jean-Luc Melenchon of the France Unbowed party, or LFI, who has joined the protests, could also face backlash if anger grows over the destruction, further handing Le Pen a stronger platform.

How did the far right gain ground after previous protests?

Right-wing and centrist parties have historically gained after mass protests and disorder as people, fearing anarchy, vote for them.

In May 1968, similar student-led protests erupted after millions of students and striking workers rallied against poor schooling conditions, increasing economic inequalities and stagnant wages.

Left-wing communist and socialist political parties joined the protests and called for a revolution. Then-President Charles de Gaulle’s conservative government initially struggled to control the demonstrations, even escaping to a French base in West Germany for a few days as violence spiralled and the country ground to a standstill.

However, the protest soon lost momentum amid the shutdown of public services. De Gaulle dissolved parliament and called for snap elections in June 1968, blaming the left for the violence and promising to restore order. His conservative Union for the Defence of the Republic party went on to win in an astounding landslide while left-wing parties lost more than half their seats.

Again, during the 2018 “yellow vest” demonstrations, working-class protesters rallying against Macron’s government’s decision to raise taxes found support among Le Pen’s party, although the left wing also tried to ingratiate itself with the movement.

Many of the movement’s supporters ended up voting for Le Pen’s party in the 2022 legislative elections to punish the Macron government, a move that still shapes the deeply divided parliament.

articles.title: Liam Payne fans flock to Wolverhampton two years after his death
articles.summary: Tributes from as far away as New Zealand are being left at a memorial in the singer's home city.
articles.body:
A memorial has been set up in tribute to One Direction star Liam Payne to mark the second anniversary of his death.

Fans from as far as New Zealand and the US have left heartfelt messages in honour of the singer in his home city of Wolverhampton.

The bandstand in West Park has been adorned with banners, photos, toys and flowers as well as a red letter box for private messages to be left.

The 31-year-old singer, who grew up in Bushbury in Wolverhampton, died in October 2024 after falling from a hotel balcony in Argentina.

Among the tributes, Kim from the US wrote: "I still can't believe it's been two years. I miss your smile, your voice, your music and just seeing you happy.

"You are still thought of, still talked about, still listened to and still loved by so many."

Katja Tuovila, from Sweden, said in an emotional message: "Your strength and love, kindness touched so many and will never be forgotten, remaining a beautiful legacy."

Nicola Jones from New Zealand added: "Two years gone but never forgotten. Always loved, forever missed. Liam, our angel of light."

In May, a coroner said he was awaiting developments in Argentina as the investigation there continues into Payne's death.

He died of multiple traumas and "internal and external haemorrhage", a post-mortem examination report said, after falling from a third-floor balcony of the Casa Sur Hotel in Buenos Aires.

In February last year, a court in Argentina dropped charges of criminal negligence against three of the five people accused of a connection to his death.

After his band took a break, Payne launched a successful solo career, releasing his debut solo album LP1 in December 2019.

articles.title: US airman dies as daredevil descent goes wrong before Texas college football game
articles.summary: The game continued after the incident. The American Conference said the decision was made before his death was known.
articles.body:
A member of the US Air Force died after he fell while abseiling from the ceiling of a Texas stadium ahead of a college football game.

Footage shows the serviceman plummet feet first to the turf midfield at San Antonio's 170ft (52 metre) high Alamodome on Saturday during a ceremony ahead of the game between the University of Texas at San Antonio and the Naval Academy.

The airman, identified by the military as Sgt Ian Patterson, a Tactical Air Control Party instructor at Joint Base San Antonio, died in hospital.

The incident is being investigated. The game between the UTSA Roadrunners and the Navy Midshipmen continued as planned following the tragic incident.

A collegiate athletic association said the decision to press ahead with the fixture was made before the airman's death had been confirmed.

"We extend our deepest condolences to his family, friends, teammates and members of the 57th Wing," the American Conference said in a statement.

US Air Force Brig Gen Scott Mills said in a statement issued by Nellis Air Force Base: "This tragedy is felt deeply across the 57th Wing.

"Tech Sgt Patterson and his service mattered immensely to our wing."

Patterson, from Fort Stewart, Georgia, had served in the US military for 15 years, according to Nellis Air Force Base.

He held multiple military decorations and was in 2022 named the Air Force Special Warfare Enlisted Instructor of the Year at the Headquarters Air Force level.

UTSA president Taylor Eighmy said: "I want to extend my deepest and most heartfelt sympathies to the service member's family, his fellow airmen, squadron and all those whose lives have been touched by this heartbreaking tragedy."

articles.title: Alberta holds non-binding separation vote as independence fight grips Canada
articles.summary: About 3 million Albertans are eligible to vote in the non-binding separation referendum, but polls show deep divisions within the UCP over it.
articles.body: OTTAWA: Residents of Alberta began voting Monday in a non-binding referendum that will determine whether the western-Canadian province should pursue separation from Canada. The vote comes at a time when the province is mourning the deaths of four soldiers, while dozens of others were injured from a fast-moving fire that burned through a military base in Alberta. While the results of a poll involving 1,021 respondents released by Abacus Data on Saturday showed that 74% of decided voters favor Alberta remaining within the Canadian Confederation, the independence issue won’t disappear for the nearly 30% who want Alberta’s government to begin the process to hold a binding provincial referendum on whether Alberta should separate from Canada, according to veteran separatist organizer Cory Morgan, who leads a group called Pathway to Independence. "It will say that about one in three Albertans have had it," Morgan told Fox News Digital. "There is a big rift within Alberta and if things don’t change, it will be a growing faction in this province — so this vote is an important one." EXCLUSIVE: ‘BROKEN COUNTRY’ FILMMAKER WARNS CANADA’S SLOW DECLINE OFFERS CAUTIONARY TALE FOR AMERICANS About 3 million Albertans are eligible to vote in the referendum. Another recent Abacus poll found that 61% of the 1,021 eligible voters surveyed expect Albertans will vote again on separation, even if most choose to remain in Canada. On Friday, the Angus Reid Institute released the results of its poll that found 62% of 1,010 Albertans surveyed believe "there will never be an end to the separatist movement" in the province. Morgan, who led the short-lived Alberta Independence Party from 2000 to 2001, said that while "a vocal minority" within the separatist movement favor Alberta becoming the 51st state, most pro-independence Albertans "don’t want to become a small fish in an even bigger pond." He added that "Albertans in general are not too thrilled with President Trump right now and that makes them less inclined to leave the federation." At a "Forever Canadian" rally on Friday in Edmonton, where he was raised, Prime Minister Mark Carney told a crowd of over 5,000 people that "this referendum comes at the worst possible time." He said that "the world is becoming more dangerous and divided [and] some outside our borders are working to break us so they can own us," making an indirect reference to Trump’s trade war against and annexation talk about Canada. Alberta-born and raised, 55-year-old Morgan said that his home province is "politically and culturally different" than eastern Canada. "There’s a lot more focus on individual freedoms and property rights," he noted, acknowledging that those values are traditionally viewed as American. "Most Albertans are going to feel much more comfortable sitting down for a beer with people from Great Falls, Montana, than they would in Ottawa," said Morgan. He explained that when Alberta became a Canadian province in 1905, its population grew largely from a migration of Montanans, and when oil was discovered in the 1940s, U.S. companies Chevron and Mobil helped develop what became Alberta’s biggest industry. Also, earlier this year during an appearance on Real America’s Voice at Davos, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent described Alberta as "a natural partner for the U.S." and described Albertans as "very independent people." In response, Carney said that he "expect[ed] the U.S. administration to respect Canadian sovereignty." Earlier this month, The Globe and Mail reported that Alberta separatist leaders met with Republican strategists in Calgary in January to look at software designed to identify and mobilize supporters. Separatist leaders also reportedly suggested exchanging water and oil for U.S. support when they met with State Department officials in Washington last year. CANADIAN PM TELLS TRUMP TO 'STOP TRYING TO BE TOUGH' IN TRADE FIGHT Alberta Premier Danielle Smith told CBC News that if most Albertans support staying in Canada, she would not hold another referendum on the matter as long as she heads the provincial government. However, on Oct. 18, 2027, residents of the province will vote again in a general election, and Smith could be out of her job by then, warned Morgan, a founding member of the former conservative Wildrose Party, for which Smith served as leader. That party merged with the then-Progressive Conservative Party of Alberta in 2020 to form the United Conservative Party (UCP) that Smith heads. But Morgan explained that more than half of the UCP’s nearly 55,000 members support Alberta’s independence. The premier has said that she will vote to keep the province in Canada. Angus Reid, founder and chairman of the Angus Reid Institute, told Fox News Digital that in his firm’s recent polling, 67% of the 293 UCP voters who support a future binding referendum on separation said that they would either "definitely support" or "consider" supporting the creation of a separatist provincial political party – not unlike the Parti Québécois, which won the recent election in Quebec. The emergence of an independence party in Alberta "would probably spell the death of the UCP since it is so badly divided between separatists and non-separatists, and it would likely end the career of Danielle Smith because of the amount of breakage in her party," said Reid, whose firm’s survey found that 60% of the respondents who support a future binding referendum are "more likely sending a message to Ottawa" about the Canadian government’s often fractious relationship with Alberta. "Separatist types are looking at how much leverage Quebec has been able to achieve in Canada as a result of its threats of exiting, and saying ‘Hold it, we can play that game too,’" explained Reid. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP As of Saturday, more than 1.2 million Albertans had cast a ballot on the referendum, which, in addition to the question on separation, has nine others, five focusing on immigration, such as one asking voters whether their province should take more control "for the purposes of decreasing immigration to more sustainable levels, prioritizing economic migration and giving Albertans first priority on new employment opportunities."

articles.title: Guernsey hospitality leader praises work permit-holder extension
articles.summary: People on a three-year work licence can now apply for a nine-month extension.
articles.body:
Guernsey hospitality industry leaders have praised the decision to relax rules around short-term employment permits, but added it "doesn't solve" immediate pressure of staff leaving next year.

Home Affairs bosses announced on Friday anyone on a three-year licence could apply for a nine-month extension.

At the time, committee president Marc Leadbeater said members made the move as they were "sympathetic" with challenges faced by employers when it came to work permits.

But, with thousands of population management applications still outstanding, the Guernsey Hospitality Association said the government should "concentrate on the critical cases like staff leaving soon".

Alan Sillett, president and director of the Guernsey Hospitality Association, said: "This is a positive outcome. But it doesn't solve all of our problems because we have immediate pressures of next year with staff having to leave just as the holiday season begins."

States Chief Executive Boley Smillie announced the government's internal audit team would be reviewing the work of population management after it was revealed that, as of 17 September , 3,886 population management applications were outstanding, alongside 324 applications within immigration workstreams.

Sillett told BBC Radio Guernsey that, as a result of the backlog, it could take "anywhere from four months to a year" to recruit staff and get them to the island for work.

He said: "It is a testing, difficult situation for our industry, and it's been growing for while.

"There have been some businesses where the owners are tearing their hair out because of the delays in the system."

However, he added that the Home Affairs Committee should be given "a little bit of time" to sort the backlog.

Sillet said: "The positive thing is they now have this as their number one priority.

"I think we need to give them a little bit of time, and if we can find a way to concentrate on the critical places like staff leaving soon, that would be good."

Home Affairs has previously said it expected the backlog within population management to be "stabilised" during 2027, "bringing greater certainty around permit processing times".

The committee said it had looked as part of its work at extending permits to a full four years or longer.

However, it said that "would likely mean a greater risk of short-term permit holders reaching a point where they may become eligible for settlement due to their length of residency or on human rights grounds".

Currently Home Affairs is reviewing the island's population policy, with that review set to be published before the end of 2027.

articles.title: DOJ official defends Trump's noncitizen voter probe on '60 Minutes,' accuses show of editing out her answers
articles.summary: Harmeet Dhillon pushed back on claims the Trump administration is sowing election distrust, saying thousands of noncitizen voting cases are under review.
articles.body: Assistant Attorney General Harmeet Dhillon defended the Trump administration's investigation into noncitizen voters ahead of the midterm elections during CBS' "60 Minutes" on Sunday. "There are people who feel that the point is to sow distrust about the whole election system. There are very few people who are noncitizens who end up voting — very, very few. And so, therefore, what's the purpose?" Lesley Stahl, host of "60 Minutes," asked Dhillon. ELECTION CRIME ARRESTS KEEP PILING UP AS DEMS INSIST IT 'JUST DOESN'T HAPPEN' Dhillon responded, "The point is actually the opposite of what you were saying. It's not to sow distrust. The distrust is there. And so, all of these kinds of crimes are being prosecuted now for the first time really, in volume. And look, even the Biden administration prosecuted 13 people for noncitizen voting." Stahl interrupted and said the numbers were "tiny." "So Lesley, we've been in office for less than two years. We've had investigations ongoing for over a year, and it takes time. There are literally thousands of them out there that we are looking at," Dhillon responded. DEMOCRATIC NEW JERSEY GOVERNOR SAYS THOUSANDS OF NONCITIZENS DISCOVERED ON VOTER ROLLS, PURGED Dhillon pledged in July that the Trump administration will pursue every provable case of illegal voting under what she described as a "broken windows" enforcement strategy, marking a sharp shift from prior administrations as the DOJ intensifies scrutiny of voter rolls following revelations that noncitizens were registered to vote in New Jersey. Dhillon told Fox News Digital at the time the department's approach is to investigate every credible lead and prosecute every case supported by the evidence, rejecting what she described as the prior view that only widespread fraud or election-altering misconduct warranted federal action. Her statement came after Democratic New Jersey Gov. Mikie Sherrill revealed that thousands of noncitizens ended up on the state's voter rolls through the motor-voter system. The "60 Minutes" host asked if there were plans to send Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents to polling locations. Dhillon said there were "no plans" to do so. Dhillon dismissed concerns that President Donald Trump would challenge the results of the midterms as "paranoia," Stahl said during a voice-over moment in the segment. The "60 Minutes" host asked Dhillon, "So would you consider a noncitizen voting an irregularity that would lead to a challenge of the vote?" Stahl went on to ask if Dhillon could rule out a challenge to a state vote. "Well, I don't know what is going to happen, but I can tell you that absent some shocking contingency that is unexpected, there should be no interruption in the usual course of counting and certifying the results in the states," Dhillon responded. "Every illegal vote cancels out the vote of a lawful American citizen," a DOJ spokesperson said in a statement to Fox News Digital. "In 2020, Iowa's 2nd Congressional District race was decided by six votes. The Department is now bringing more than double that amount of election fraud cases every week. Every federal race also shares the ballot with state and local contests, which are often decided by even narrower margins. Voting by noncitizens and other ineligible voters is a federal crime, and the Department will enforce the law whether a case involves one illegal ballot or hundreds. articles.title: Elon Musk and Anthropic make promises to give the public a piece of the AI pie
articles.summary: Elon Musk and officials at AI giant Anthropic are pledging to give coveted shares in their companies to the general public as concerns about AI’s economic and societal impact continue to pile up.
articles.body: Elon Musk and officials at AI giant Anthropic are pledging to give coveted shares in their companies to the general public as concerns about AI’s economic and societal impact continue to pile up. “Next year, I will give one of my SpaceX shares to every kid in America,” Musk posted on X on Monday. “This will be the first of many.” One SpaceX share is currently valued at about $150. With approximately 72 million children under the age of 18 in the U.S., Musk’s donation would currently be worth about $10.8 billion — less than 2% of his current net worth. He provided no additional information. Musk could not be reached for additional comment. His statement comes one day after officials at Anthropic said the company would commit 5% of company shares to a “public benefit fund” in order to address “labor market impacts” of AI.In a statement, Anthropic officials said the fund could make charitable donations or direct money to “specific populations,” emphasizing the fund’s “versatility.” “Given the pace of AI progress, bolder approaches may be needed,” they said. Anthropic has been preparing for an initial public offering — releasing its stock for trading on public markets — that analysts say would value the company at more than $1 trillion. The company has long championed employees’ charitable giving by promising to match their donations. Musk replied to Anthropic on X saying it should give shares “directly to the public.” While evidence of AI’s impact on work so far remains mixed, a core premise underlying the current artificial intelligence investment boom is that it will make business processes vastly more efficient, including by eroding returns to human labor. That’s prompted fears about exacerbating income inequality and sparked worries of a “permanent underclass” forming throughout society. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has been at the forefront of such warnings, predicting that 50% of all white-collar work could be eliminated by AI before the end of the decade. An Associated Press poll published last week found 64% of U.S. adults believe AI is developing “too fast,” with 8 in 10 saying the government should prioritize protecting the country’s workforce. A separate NBC News survey published last month found 70% of Americans are more worried than excited about AI, with a majority stating they would oppose construction of a data center in their neighborhood. Notably, even before the advent of current advanced AI models, labor’s share of economic growth had been seeing precipitous declines. The Trump administration has sought to bridge some of that gap by seeding financial accounts for children born starting in 2025 with $1,000. Other high-profile business people have pledged additional amounts to the accounts, including SpaceX President and COO Gwynne Shotwell, who along with her husband planned to give money to 2 million children in low-income areas, especially in Texas. Musk has made numerous bold statements in his career only to subsequently not follow through on them. Among the most high-profile was his August 2018 announcement that he had “secured” funding to take Tesla private. The transaction failed to materialize and cost Musk his chairmanship of Tesla.

articles.title: Who is cult head Paul Mackenzie, convicted of convincing followers to die?
articles.summary: A Kenyan court has handed down the first judgement in the ‘doomsday’ cult case.
articles.body:
A court in the Kenyan city of Mombasa has found a self-proclaimed pastor and his associates guilty of the murder of 191 people, all but one of whom were children.

Paul Mackenzie and several of his followers were charged with murder after his cult was alleged to have forced children to starve so they could “meet Jesus”.

Before Monday’s verdict, the accused had pleaded not guilty and also denied charges in other cases, including terrorism, radicalisation and stopping children from attaining an education.

Mackenzie was the head of the apocalyptic Good News International Ministries, which he established with his wife in 2003 in the southeastern coastal city of Malindi. Before that, he was a taxi driver in Nairobi.

The church drew thousands of followers across its many branches in Kenya, with devotees also following Mackenzie’s fiery sermons broadcast on the church television station, Times TV.

He reportedly convinced followers he could speak to God. Some of them are believed to have sold off property to donate to the church.

Mackenzie preached doomsday conspiracy theories of education as being “evil”, with children forbidden from attending school. He banned his followers from using medication because it was against religious “doctrine” and encouraged followers to burn birth certificates and digital IDs. His preaching was also anti-Western, including condemnation of the United States, the United Nations and even the Catholic Church.

Authorities began to scrutinise Mackenzie’s establishment in the late 2010s.

After his church and TV station were forced to shut down in 2019, he moved to the Shakahola forest in Kilifi County, about 70 kilometres (43.4 miles) from Malindi. Some of his devotees relocated with him to live in mud houses in the vast forest.

In 2023, authorities were tipped off by a man whose wife and daughter had also relocated to the remote forest.

Police investigations led to shallow mass graves in the forest linked to the cult group. Authorities also found dozens of other emaciated surviving members in the forest. Some told police that Mackenzie had ordered them to starve themselves until they “meet Jesus”.

Most of the bodies exhumed were of children. Some of the victims also died of strangulation or blunt trauma, authorities said, adding that some people who tried to leave the cult were attacked. Others were found with their hands and legs bound together.

A total of 429 deaths were reported, including many others who later died in hospital. Hundreds are still declared missing.

Mackenzie is not believed to have starved himself. Survivors said that according to his orders, children were to starve themselves, followed by unmarried women, men, and last of all, church leaders.

Authorities accused Mackenzie of instigating a mass starvation campaign that led to the deaths. In January 2024, Mackenzie was charged with 191 counts of murder and his church was proscribed as an “organised criminal group”.

Mackenzie, along with 34 others, including other leaders of the church, were arrested and charged with murder and terrorism-related offences.

Enos Amanya Ngala, Mackenzie’s former head of security, was one of the accused, but he entered a guilty plea deal and agreed to stand as a witness for the prosecution.

At a 2024 hearing at the Kenya High Court, the court urged prosecutors to reduce the charges to 12 to speed up the process. Mackenzie and his colleagues pleaded not guilty to the crimes.

Officials also initially arraigned 65 rescued victims on charges of attempted suicide, which carries a two-year sentence in Kenya. A court in Mombasa ordered they be remanded in a rescue centre and monitored, after many reportedly rejected food.

While in jail, Mackenzie was accused of involvement in another 52 deaths after officials said he was luring more victims to their deaths by writing notes from his prison cell.

articles.title: Famine fears as aid cuts and shipment restrictions coincide in Gaza
articles.summary: Displaced families in Gaza fear worsening food insecurity as planned aid cuts coincide with continued restrictions.
articles.body:
Deir el-Balah, Gaza Strip — Manal Abu Rabie, a displaced mother of six from Beit Lahiya in northern Gaza, received news that the World Food Programme (WFP) was cutting food assistance to the enclave with fear about what is to follow in the coming days.

Gaza has suffered from severe shortages of key staples such as eggs, flour and onions after Israel closed border crossings into the enclave on Wednesday. The prices of food and other essentials have skyrocketed, and families who can afford to do so have been bulk buying, in anticipation of a prolonged blockade.

After the WFP announced cuts to food aid, the price of a bundle of bread rose from 5 to 12 shekels (around $1.60 to $3.90).

Abu Rabie has already been struggling to provide food for her family and says she has little to fall back on if the support she needs is reduced after the announcement of aid cuts.

“We were just beginning to say, ‘Thank God,’ and now they want to cut off our food and drink,” she said. “We are going back to starvation. We are dying of hunger.”

On Monday, the WFP announced that a funding shortfall had forced it to reduce the number of people receiving monthly food assistance in Gaza from 1.6 million to 1.1 million, leaving around 500,000 people without support.

The agency is also halving food rations, meaning families receiving assistance will get one food parcel instead of two, alongside a smaller bag of wheat flour.

The number of hot meals provided daily will fall from 250,000 to 150,000, while cash assistance will be reduced for 75,000 families. The WFP said the cuts were driven by a lack of funding, despite continued humanitarian needs.

The suspension of aid shipments into Gaza for a sixth consecutive day, which is a separate development, has added to uncertainty about the availability and affordability of food, fuel and medicine.

Abu Rabie, 39, who lives in al-Salam camp in Deir el-Balah, central Gaza, relies on food assistance, including parcels containing lentils, rice, flour and cooking oil.

Her family is already struggling to afford basic food items as prices rise, with a small bottle of cooking oil, which is included in WFP food parcels, now costing 10 shekels ($3.20), is beyond her means.

“It is very difficult. I cannot afford to buy anything,” she said.

She has high blood pressure, diabetes and heart disease. With no alternative, she is forced to live off the food provided in aid parcels, aggravating her digestive problems.

“If the assistance stops and the quantities become smaller, how are we supposed to get through the day? We’ll have to eat sand. That is all that will be left for us,” she said.

“I swear to God, my son asks me for things, and I cannot get them for him. My husband is injured, and I am sick.”

The approaching winter is adding to her anxiety. Abu Rabie said her family had no blankets or mattresses.

“I say, ‘God, please don’t let winter come’, because we have no blankets and no mattresses,” she said. “There is no food and no drink. God knows how we are managing.”

In a statement issued on Monday, Gaza’s Government Media Office warned that the WFP’s planned cuts could worsen the humanitarian crisis and leave hundreds of thousands of Palestinians facing greater food insecurity.

The office called on the United Nations and the international community to provide urgent funding to sustain relief programmes. It also held Israel responsible for the consequences of the restrictions on aid entering Gaza, and called for all crossings to be opened to allow humanitarian supplies to enter without interruption.

The statement urged Arab and Islamic countries, as well as international organisations, to provide financial support and help facilitate the delivery of food, medical supplies and other essential items.

The WFP, meanwhile, has attributed its planned reductions to a funding shortfall rather than a decline in humanitarian needs, appealing to donors for additional support.

Randa al-War, a displaced mother of three originally from Gaza City’s Shujayea neighbourhood, said food assistance from the WFP is a lifeline.

She now lives with her family in Sarsour camp in Deir el-Balah and said they receive no assistance from other organisations.

“We depend on the World Food Programme. We cannot live without bread, without flour. These children need to eat,” she said.

Al-War said the food parcels which her family receives every two or three months, including flour and cooking oil, last around a month.

“We get through the day if the food parcel comes. If it comes, the children eat. If it doesn’t, there is no food,” she said.

She fears that the WFP’s cuts could leave her family without the support it relies on. Buying food from the market is not a realistic alternative, she said, because neither she nor her husband can work as she is injured and he has health problems.

“I cannot work, and my husband cannot work,” she said. “We are living only on the World Food Programme and the food parcels.”

Al-War said the prospect of further cuts has left her frightened that her children will face hunger again.

“We are afraid there will be famine, because of our children. We will not be able to provide them with anything,” she said. “We are not just afraid… we are terrified that famine will return.”

Rising prices add to families’ struggles

The suspension of commercial shipments is adding to the pressure on families already struggling with reduced purchasing power and rising prices caused by the war and Israel’s siege on Gaza.

Rami al-Zayigh, a Gaza-based economic expert, said the continued closure of crossings was restricting the supply of goods in a territory already facing persistent shortages, pushing prices higher and placing further pressure on families.

“The issue goes beyond a shortage of supply,” al-Zayigh said. “Whenever the crossings close, traders and sellers raise prices, creating panic among citizens. The citizen is the biggest victim of these measures.”

Vegetables and fruit were becoming scarce in local markets, and the price of eggs had risen by about 300 percent over the past week.

Vegetables and fruit are particularly vulnerable to interruptions in supply as they risk spoiling within days, al-Zayigh said.

Citing official reports from Gaza, he said food stocks in the territory were estimated to be sufficient for only about two weeks. He warned that continued restrictions on goods entering Gaza could have further economic and health consequences, particularly for children and older people.

For families who rely on aid, the combination of reduced assistance, limited income and higher prices leaves fewer ways to secure daily meals. Al-War said families should not have to beg for the essentials they need to survive.

“We want to live like the rest of the world. We do not want to beg for these things. They should be available to us without us having to ask,” she said.

“We are human beings. We want to live, eat and drink. We want a dignified life.”

articles.title: In pictures: French landmarks damaged and destroyed by violent protesters
articles.summary: France is used to protests but the violence and damage seen across the country is shocking many people.
articles.body:
Local curfews may come into force in French towns following a weekend of disorder.

Most of the protesters were peaceful in expressing their opposition to rising fuel prices, the cost of living and deteriorating public services, including schools.

But others - dressed in black and wearing masks and balaclavas - set fire to cars, shops and buildings.

The scale of the destruction - including to some iconic landmarks - has shocked many in a country used to street protests.

The damage in the capital city is extensive. Shop fronts have been broken and stores looted.

The iconic Place de la Republique was vandalised, too.

A yellow vest - representative of the movement which helped co-ordinate the weekend protests - was draped around the body of the Statue of the Republic, erected in 1883.

Groups of rioters, some dressed in black and wearing masks and balaclavas, took over parts of the capital and wreaked havoc.

Tear gas and stun grenades were fired at hundreds of people but police struggled to contain smaller groups of people roving around the city attack businesses.

The full extent of the damage did not become clear until dawn broke on Sunday.

Further south in Marseille, protesters broke into the city hall by using a metal fence as a battering ram.

A bust of Marianne - symbol of the French Republic - was damaged and knocked to the floor in Marseille as people ransacked the building.

City Mayor Benoît Payan was furious with the "almost total lack of control" by the security forces.

"The world's sixth largest power does not deserve this. The world is watching us, this morning we are the shame of Europe," he said.

In the city of Lyon, Mayor Grégory Doucet said the burning of the city's tourist office, housed in a 19th Century building, was "a tragedy".

Fire crews also battled a fire at Limoges town hall, which caused part of the building to collapse. Local officials said the town hall was "largely lost".

"A wild horde" had "deliberately" set fire to the 143-year-old building, said Maurice Barate, the prefect for the Haute-Vienne department.

French authorities have admitted they lost control of cities to the protesters.

Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez offered his resignation - which has been rejected.

Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu has given local mayors the power to introduce partial curfews in some parts of the country, which he says is designed to protect people and businesses.

But the French are holding their breath - in anticipation of another chapter in this protest next Saturday.
