articles.title: Why experts say weighted stuffed animals are the ultimate calming tool for anxiety
articles.summary: According to research, weighted stuffed animals can decrease anxiety and leave you feeling calmer. Here are the best options to shop.
articles.body: Research has shown that a weighted blanket can help decrease anxiety. And while it can be a good option if you’re lounging on the couch or in bed, it’s not exactly the easiest item to move around with. That’s where weighted stuffed animals come in. They’re lighter, more portable and cuter. The best part? They offer similar calming benefits and are a great option for kids, although anyone can use them, says Lynelle Schneeberg, a licensed clinical psychologist and assistant professor at the Yale School of Medicine. I spoke with experts to find out what you should know about weighted stuffed animals — including what research actually says about the benefits and what to know before buying one. I also rounded up a handful of highly-rated options to purchase for yourself or a loved one, some of which NBC Selected staff members tested. Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter. The best weighted stuffed animals The weighted stuffed animals below come in multiple styles, so if you’re looking for something specific, like a certain color or animal, browse the websites of the various brands. To come up with this list, I relied on recommendations from NBC Selected editors, as well as highly-rated options that meet the criteria provided by our experts. Editor’s pick NBC Selected editorial operations associate Jem Alabi says this Hugz weighted stuffed animal has become an emotional support toy for her. “I like to carry her on my hip while walking around and I wrap her around myself while working at my desk,” she says (the brand sent her a sample to test). “I find that her weight and softness help ground me, making it easier to focus. The office can get pretty cold, so I love that I can put her in the microwave for a couple seconds to make her warm. When summer comes, I can’t wait to put her in the freezer for a while and snuggle with her while sleeping to help cool me down as a night sweater.” Alabi says the highland cow shed a lot when it came out of the box, so she recommends using a sticky roller to remove excess fuzz before using it. She has the standard size weighted stuffed cow that’s 3.8 pounds and 10 inches tall, but if you want something smaller, Hugz makes a mini version that’s 2.2 pounds and is 8 inches tall. Best for kids of all ages One of the most popular weighted stuffed animals brands, Warmies offers dozens of weighted stuffed animals in various sizes, weights, styles and characters. For example, Warmies has a weighted elephant, frog, cat and more. The brand also offers a junior line, which includes smaller weighted stuffed animals that could be a good option for younger kids. Each stuffed animal is filled with flaxseed and dried lavender to promote relaxation, according to the brand. You can also place them in the microwave and freezer. NBC Selected commerce editor Bethany Heitman bought a Warmie’s junior rainbow dinosaur for her 4-year-old daughter to use before bed. “If my daughter is having a hard time settling down for the night, I’ll pop this dinosaur — she’s named it Sparkles — in the microwave for a few minutes,” says Heitman. “Then, she snuggles with it while we do story time and she almost instantly calms down.” Best machine-washable Hugimals’ weighted stuffed animals have a removable pouch of non-toxic glass beads that give it heft. You can easily remove the pouch and machine wash the plush cover whenever you need to. In addition to Darby the Bear, Hugimals sells other weighted stuffed animals like Charlie the Puppy, Frankie the Cat and Harper the Pig. They also have a newer option called a Hugaround, which has long, weighted arms that you can wrap around you to mimic the feeling of a hug. The brand sent me the koala to test and I was impressed by its overall construction. It’s plush enough to feel cozy, yet firm enough to sit up on its own. The fabric exterior is soft against my skin, too. At 4.5 pounds, I felt light pressure on my legs when I placed the weighted stuffed animal on my lap, but it would still be manageable for kids to tote around. Best heavy weighted stuffed animal The weight of this pink axolotl is distributed across six zones, so it offers even pressure no matter how you hug or snuggle with it. The stuffed animal is filled with glass beads that don’t make any sound as they move, according to the brand. Because of the heavier weight, it may not be suitable for small children. Best budget weighted stuffed animal This weighted stuffed turtle weighs 4.5 pounds and is filled with small beads. The brand also makes smaller animals that weigh a pound, which is a good choice for young children and larger animals that weigh five pounds. The animals are machine washable and can be placed outside in the sun to dry, according to the brand. Best weighted stuffed animal alternative Feel silly snuggling up with a stuffed animal? Bearaby’s Hugget — an NBC Selected Wellness Award winner — provides a nice alternative. I own one and hug it whenever I’m lounging on the couch, plus I keep it out in my living room at all times because its knot design doubles as a piece of home decor. The weighted pillow is made from Melofoam, a plant-based material, and is covered in an organic cotton fabric. Bearaby’s Huggets are also approved by the American Chiropractic Association (ACA). It is also available in two sizes — medium or large. What are the wellness benefits of weighted stuffed animals? Similar to weighted blankets, research shows that the benefits of weighted stuffed animals center around something called deep pressure therapy, which involves asserting gentle pressure on the body to induce feeling safe, cozy and calm. “They both provide pressure the same way a hug, massage or baby swaddle would,” says Schneeberg. And while people anecdotally say weighted blankets and weighted stuffed animals make them feel less anxious or stressed, as well as help them sleep, there’s no hard research supporting one or the other, says Dr. Alex Dimitriu, a board-certified psychiatrist and sleep medicine specialist and founder of Menlo Park Psychiatry & Sleep Medicine. With this in mind, best way to see if a weighted stuffed animal could work for you is to try one. How to shop for a weighted stuffed animal If you’d like to invest in a weighted stuffed animal, consider the following criteria when shopping: Weight: Most weighted stuffed animals weigh between one pound and 5 pounds. If you are buying a stuffed animal for yourself or another adult, choose one based on your personal preference. However, if you are shopping for a child, you’ll want to select a weight that they can easily pick up on their own, says Schneeberg.Fabric type: The whole point of a weighted stuffed animal is to cuddle with it, so look for options made from fabric that’s soft and non-irritating against the skin, says Dimitriu. The material should also be breathable so it doesn’t make you too warm, he says.Additional comforting benefits: Some weighted stuffed animals can also be used as a heating or cooling pad to be even more soothing. Usually, this means the stuffed animal or a removable piece can be put in the microwave or freezer. The stuffed animal will usually retain that temperature for only a short amount of time, says Schneeberg.Return policy: Weighted stuffed animals make a great gift for yourself or loved ones, but if the weight doesn’t wind up feeling quite right or there’s another issue, you’ll want to be able to return or exchange it. Meet our wellness experts At NBC Selected, we work with experts who have specialized knowledge and authority based on relevant training and/or experience. We also take steps to ensure that all expert advice and recommendations are made independently and with no undisclosed financial conflicts of interest. Lynelle Schneeberg is a licensed clinical psychologist and assistant professor at the Yale School of Medicine. She’s also a fellow at the American Academy of Sleep Medicine and author of “Become Your Child’s Sleep Coach: The Bedtime Doctor’s 5-Step Guide, Ages 3-10.”Dr. Alex Dimitriu is double board-certified in psychiatry and sleep medicine. He is the founder of Menlo Park Psychiatry & Sleep Medicine and BrainfoodMD. Why trust NBC Selected? I am a reporter at NBC Selected who writes about a range of wellness topics, including stories on wedge pillows, anti-snoring devices, slippers, sleep masks and sunrise alarm clocks. For this article, I interviewed two experts about weighted stuffed animals and rounded up highly rated options, as well as those NBC Selected staff tested. Catch up on NBC Selected’s in-depth coverage of tech and tools, wellness and more, and follow us on Facebook, Instagram, X and TikTok to stay up to date.

articles.title: Indian court extends detention of ‘Cockroach’ leaders
articles.summary: The extension of the custody of the CJP activists comes amid a crackdown on near daily protests against the government.
articles.body:
An Indian ‌‌court has extended the detention of two leaders of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP).

The extension for Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das on Monday comes amid a crackdown on near-daily protests against the government.

The two activists from the youth-led movement were arrested as they demonstrated at a historic protest venue despite a ban. Their jailing provoked a new protest in New Delhi on Friday.

The CJP is a major force behind the protests, which have demanded the resignation of India’s election chief over a controversial revision of voter lists that critics say favours Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Bharatiya ⁠⁠Janata Party (BJP).

Ranka and Das were ⁠⁠among 14 protesters who climbed over barricades last week to enter the Jantar Mantar observatory, the day after it was removed from a list of approved demonstration sites. A court later sent the activists to prison for five days.

Indian media reported on Monday evening that they had been detained for two more days after police requested extra time to question them. Delhi ‌‌Police did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

“This is an absolute mockery of the judicial system,” the CJP’s legal head, Ratna Singh, told reporters outside the court, adding that the party would challenge the order in a higher court.

The CJP, alongside opposition parties and left-wing student organisations, has led near-daily protests this month demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation, after 130 million names were removed from voter lists.

The Election Commission has said that the lists included 28 million people who have died, 63 million who have relocated, and 30 million who could not be traced. It denied favouring any party and said ⁠⁠wrongly deleted voters can re-enrol.

The BJP has accused rivals of trying to undermine democracy by wrongly questioning legitimate electoral processes.

CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke , student leaders and several of their supporters were also detained on Friday as ⁠⁠hundreds poured into central Delhi for a protest in support of Das and Ranka.

However, the youth-led movement insists it will not back off. A sit-in by the CJP and its supporters earlier this year forced the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over exam paper leaks.

articles.title: Hungary and Poland defend tough migration policies as France reels from violent unrest
articles.summary: Violent unrest in France and Italy fuels the migration debate as Hungary and Poland defend tougher border controls and warn Europe against repeating past mistakes.
articles.body: As images of burning cars and historic buildings in France and Italy ricochet across Europe, leaders in Hungary and Poland are seizing the moment, not to address the unrest, but to redefine the migration debate. Both Hungary and Poland have laid down markers on allowing migrants into their nations. Even to the point of being fined and sanctioned by the European Union courts for refusing to open their gates to unchecked immigration, in Hungary’s case under former Prime Minister Viktor Orbán, while Poland faced sanctions in 2025. Eurostat’s latest available figures show that in 2025 France had almost 10 million and Italy about 7 million foreign-born residents. Poland had roughly 1 million foreign-born residents, while Hungary had less than 700,000, with most born in other EU countries and in Poland’s case about half came from Ukraine. TRUMP, WALTZ LINK FRANCE RIOTS TO MASS IMMIGRATION AS THOUSANDS ARE ARRESTED Reacting to the violence, Hungary’s Prime Minister Péter Magyar posted on X that, "Europe can count on Hungary." He stated that, "In the face of this senseless destruction and unjustified violence, perhaps it is now clear to everyone why Hungary advocates the strictest possible approach to migration, and why we will not weaken our border protection or immigration policy under any pressure." It is a sentiment echoed by Magyar’s Polish counterpart, Donald Tusk posted: "Poland will not repeat the mistakes of other European countries, nor will it pay for them," he wrote on Sunday night. "We are firmly defending the border against illegal migration, we have our own asylum policy (we do not accept applications), we deport those who break Polish law. On security issues, we will be relentless." Sweden-based political scientist Daniel Schatz told Fox News Digital, "Burning buildings and looted shops in France and other countries are becoming political ammunition across Europe… Leaders pushing tougher immigration policies have a blunt message for voters at home: ‘This is what we intend to prevent.’ Images of chaos can carry more political weight than a hundred policy speeches." According to the latest available crime statistics from Eurostat, the European Union’s official statistical office, in 2024 France reported 304,900 police-recorded offenses, among the highest totals in the EU. Italy reported 142,600, while Poland with 57,300 and Hungary’s 28,600 were among the lowest totals in Europe. This as Eurostat’s 2023 "perception metric," or what percentage of people report crime or vandalism in their areas, showed France was again among the highest with about 20%, Italy reported 14-17%, Poland 7-8%, and Hungary at 6-7%. FRENCH SCHOOL RIOTS DEEPEN AS EXPERTS POINT TO FAR-LEFT ALLIANCE FUELING ‘BROADER CONFRONTATION’ "In Central and Eastern European countries, the riots in France are linked to immigration and to the issue of non-adaptation and non-integration of immigrants," Boštjan Udovič, Chair of International Relations at the University of Ljubljana’s Faculty of Social Sciences in Slovenia, told Fox News Digital. "Magyar and Tusk are delivering a blunt message to Brussels," Schatz added, "being pro-European does not mean signing up for liberal immigration policies… Magyar explicitly presents the French disorder as vindication of his migration policy. Tusk’s warning against repeating other countries’ mistakes reinforces a similar political message." Magyar said last week’s European Council summit "made it clear that the overwhelming majority of European countries have woken up and want to break with the permissive policies of the past. We hope it is not too late. "The Europe we all love is in serious trouble today," the Hungarian leader said. "It is our responsibility, too, to help preserve our continent as the most wonderful place in the world for our children and grandchildren… I express my full solidarity with the French people." ITALY’S SCHOOL VEIL BAN EXPOSES EUROPE’S ASSIMILATION FIGHT AS EXPERT WARNS US COULD BE NEXT Schatz said Magyar and Tusk "do not need to invoke Polish King Jan Sobieski’s leadership of the allied army that broke the Ottoman siege of Vienna in 1683 — a victory long celebrated as a defense of Christian Europe — to cast themselves as Europe’s protectors. Burning buildings provide a vivid contemporary backdrop for that message." Udovič is not surprised by Magyar and Tusk’s positions, noting that Central and Eastern European countries "usually link their EU membership to their identity, based mostly on a single nation." This is part of their history, he says, and "it would be unrealistic to expect that countries that fought for their independence based on their national movement would adopt… a concept of a multiethnic society." Schatz added, "This is ‘all politics is local’ playing out across borders. The streets are French or Italian; the voters being addressed are Hungarian or Polish." Udovič noted that Tusk is entering "a sort of pre-election campaign where migration will also be an issue." MELONI CONDEMNS ‘GANGS OF THUGS’ AFTER PROTESTS TURNED VIOLENT ACROSS ITALY Poland’s next parliamentary election is slated for Nov. 2027, and former Prime Minister Mateusz Morawiecki, a possible Tusk opponent, is echoing his successor’s remarks. "France is burning, and we must be wise before the harm is done," Morawiecki posted to X Monday morning. He added that his new center-right political coalition, Rozwoj Plus, "has a package of comprehensive solutions that will allow Poland to be not only prosperous, but also the safest country in the world!" Meanwhile, "Strict immigration policies enjoy broad support in Hungary," former government official under the previous Prime Minister Viktor Orbán and current board member of the Hungarian Atlantic Council Á. Félix Debrenti told Fox News Digital. He said, "Magyar understands that abandoning Orbán’s tough approach to immigration and border protection could cost him significant political support, particularly at a time when his party is already facing growing pressures." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP He said, "Taking a strong position on immigration allows Magyar to shift public attention away from the government’s domestic challenges and onto an issue where there is a broad national consensus," Debrenti continues. "All this comes just days before Oct. 23… when Hungarians commemorate the 1956 Revolution and the fight for freedom against Soviet oppression." Touching on the protests, Magyar posted: "Let there be no doubt: peaceful and lawful protest is one thing; vandalism and violence are quite another. The former is a fundamental right; the latter is a serious crime."

articles.title: Olivia Dunne and an NFL WAG dominate the Victoria's Secret show, Aaron Rodgers goes off & the refs STINK again
articles.summary: Olivia Dunne and Kristin Juszczyk dominated the Victoria's Secret fashion show Pink Carpet while NFL and college football delivered stunning upsets.
articles.body: 'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday-Friday on OutKick.com. Third full week of October is here, boys and girls. Time to lock in. Everything is out in front of us. We're in the absolute sweet spot of football season, both college and NFL. Was that the greatest Saturday slate of all time? It may have been. Hockey is here. The NBA starts this week for those who care. The World Series is right around the corner. SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM SENDS A MESSAGE TO THE WOMAN-HATING WNBA PLAYERS WITH HER HAT, CRANKY PRIME & MAGGIE SAJAK! The WNBA is still, somehow, doing WNBA things and disrespecting our great national anthem. The weather has finally started to turn here in Florida. It ain't much, but when your highs are only 80 and not 90 on a consistent basis, it feels like winter. I only have to change shirts twice a day now! What a blessing. How lucky are we? Let's roll. Welcome to a Monday Nightcaps — the one where Olivia Dunne and an NFL WAG stole the show at last night's Victoria's Secret fashion show, which is apparently still going on. Who knew?! I didn't, but I do now. What else? It's overflowing right now! Been too long since we heard from you guys. That's on me. We'll fix it here in a bit. Grab you some chicken and waffles as we celebrate National Chicken & Waffles Day, and settle in for a Monday 'Cap! We had a big crossover event last night Normally I'm against popular trends, but I can't knock chicken and waffles. Great pairing. I've got nothing bad to say about either. Cracker Barrel, if I recall, had a solid chicken and waffle special at one point. No clue if they still do, but from what I remember, it was good. Side note: Anyone been to a Cracker Barrel lately? I know it's been a rough year for them, but I'd be curious to see if things improved over the summer after they canned that terrible CEO. Let me know! HAILEY OSTROM HITS GOLF COURSE IN MIDDLE OF HER 31 DAYS OF HALLOWEEN COSTUMES, VERONIKA RAJEK IS BACK & MEAT OK, let's go ahead and start class — and the week — with another elite pairing: Sports and Victoria's Secret fashion shows. Just last night, while the Cowboys were peeing all over themselves at Lambeau, the models were out and about at the annual show in LA. Normally, I'd say San Francisco by a billion, but after the weekend we just experienced with upsets, I'm staying away from this one. Seriously, I can't remember a weekend with more upsets between college and the NFL. Obviously, Saturday was insane. I was stunned Georgia lost. Stunned. I thought Kirby Smart was upset-proof. And how about the Colts choking yesterday against the TITANS of all teams? That one cut me especially deep, because I had the Colts in Hard Rock's $2 million survivor pool. I couldn't believe what I was watching. Unfathomable. The biggest near-upset of the weekend took place in Coral Gables Saturday night, where Miami — now the No. 1 team in the country — nearly lost to FSU. Frankly, they should have. This holding call was maybe the softest "holding" call I've ever seen in my life: Aaron, reader mail & commercials! It was just so bad. I said it at the time, and I'll say it again today: FSU was robbed. If that's a hold, they might as well just go ahead and call it on every single play. FSU vs. Miami … both of the last second plays in double OT … officials just wanted to get to their cars alive … 2 terrible calls back to back against FSU. 2 BYU/ ND … how many times is clock management going to be an issue with 12+ grown men watching a replay? articles.title: Yerawada road trench death sparks demand for culpable homicide case against contractor, officials
articles.summary: Yerawada road trench death in Pune sparks outrage; residents demand culpable homicide case against contractor and officials as PMC issues show-cause notice.
articles.body: Pune: The death of a 69-year-old man after falling into a poorly barricaded road trench in Yerawada on Sunday has sparked widespread outrage, with mounting demands for strict criminal action, including a culpable homicide case, against the contractor and officials responsible for the unsafe public works.Pradeep Laxman Pardeshi, a laundry business owner from Yerawada, had suffered serious injuries after falling into the trench and died during treatment. Citing site videos, corporator Avinash Salve had blamed flimsy barricades and demanded the contractor be permanently blacklisted and booked for culpable homicide over negligence.While Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) maintained that safety instructions were issued to contractors, residents argued that such assurances rang hollow as similar accidents continued to occur across Maharashtra, including in Mumbai and Nashik.Citizens’ groups said the tragedy highlighted a larger crisis of poor road safety, unchecked civic negligence and a lack of accountability. “Have the lives of ordinary citizens become so cheap?” asked Satara Road resident Rucha Joshi. “Walking on roads has become risky. Encroachments have already eaten into public space, footpaths are narrow and poorly executed civic works are making matters worse,” she said.Residents pointed out that pothole-ridden and damaged roads had become increasingly accident-prone, claiming several lives in recent years.Consumer rights activist Vivek Velankar alleged that civic authorities and contractors routinely ignored established standards and Indian Roads Congress norms during infrastructure projects. “Despite repeated promises of action, nothing changes on the ground. The civic administration must register criminal cases against those who have failed in their duties. Serious charges, including culpable homicide, should be invoked to create a deterrent,” he said.PMC issues notice to contractorCivic officials said legal proceedings had already been initiated against the contractor involved in the work. “The contractor has been served a show-cause notice and asked to submit an explanation within 24 hours,” Rajendra Jadhav, superintending engineer of the PMC’s drainage department, said.He said further action would be taken after examining the response and other relevant facts.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Pune | Silver Rate in Pune | Bank Holidays in Pune | Public Holidays in Pune | Petrol Price in Pune | Diesel Price in Pune | CNG Price in Pune | LPG Price in PuneStay updated with the latest Pune news. articles.title: 3rd Flyover Drags, Inner Ring Rd Takes A Beating, Motorists Stare At Two More Years of Chaos
articles.summary: Nagpur’s Manewada–Mhalgi Nagar 3-in-1 flyover delays worsen Inner Ring Road, with potholes and bottlenecks; connecting span may take 24 months.
articles.body: Nagpur: Ongoing construction of a three-in-one flyover between Manewada and Mhalgi Nagar has turned commuting on Inner Ring Road into a daily nightmare, increasing the risk of accidents. The World Bank division of the state Public Works Department (PWD) appears to have surrendered to the situation, as the road continues to deteriorate despite repeated repairs, triggering traffic snarls.Adding to commuters’ woes, construction of the crucial 1.5km connecting flyover between Manewada and Mhalgi Nagar squares is yet to begin. With a 24-month completion deadline, motorists may have to endure the chaos for another two years.A PWD official told TOI that work on the connecting flyover is likely to begin next week. “We are planning to complete the work within 18 months,” the official said.Sources, however, blamed the PWD for delaying the project. “Despite getting administrative approval in Feb 2025, PWD’s World Bank division awarded the tender for the connecting flyover in May 2026. Even five months after the tender was awarded, construction has not commenced,” sources said.Union minister Nitin Gadkari performed the bhoomipujan for two flyovers at Manewada and Mhalgi Nagar, each costing approximately ₹73 crore, in August 2024. During the ceremony, he proposed connecting the two structures to create a continuous elevated corridor.The state govt subsequently approved the connecting flyover, expanding the project into a 2.8km elevated corridor. To accommodate the revised design, PWD removed the descending ramp after Manewada Square and the ascending ramp before Mhalgi Nagar Square, allowing the three structures to merge seamlessly.However, construction of the originally planned flyovers has left motorists struggling through narrowed carriageways, barricaded stretches and damaged roads.The deteriorating road surface has compounded the problem. Despite multiple repair attempts, potholes, loose gravel and uneven stretches continue to pose serious safety hazards.According to sources, PWD has repeatedly undertaken patchwork repairs, but heavy vehicular movement prevents freshly laid bitumen from settling properly, causing repaired portions to deteriorate quickly.During peak hours, vehicles crawl through the stretch, with barricades further squeezing the available road space and creating long traffic queues.“At several places, the road is uneven and two-wheelers skid. There are also major craters, while barricades have slowed traffic considerably. We fear the situation will turn into complete chaos once construction of the connecting flyover begins,” said Mangesh Patre, a regular commuter.Project: 3-in-1 Manewada–Mhalgi Nagar Flyover.Status: Two flyovers at Manewada and Mhalgi Nagar are currently under construction, the third flyover work yet to begin.Initial Cost: The two flyovers have an administrative approval of ₹73 crore each , while their tenders were awarded for less than ₹50 crore each.Length: The combined project will create a 2.80-km continuous elevated corridor.Connecting flyover: Administrative approval of ₹185 crore; tender awarded for ₹106 crore.Tender awarded: May 15, 2026.Completion timeline: Connecting flyover has a 24-month construction period after work starts.Design changes: Descending ramp after Manewada and ascending ramp before Mhalgi Nagar were removed to create one uninterrupted flyover.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Nagpur | Silver Rate in Nagpur | Bank Holidays in Nagpur | Public Holidays in Nagpur | Petrol Price in Nagpur | Diesel Price in Nagpur | CNG Price in Nagpur | LPG Price in NagpurStay updated with the latest Nagpur news. articles.title: Florida issues arrest warrant for Cuban leader Raul Castro
articles.summary: The announcement mirrors a federal indictment from May as the US steps up pressure on the Cuban government.
articles.body:
Florida, in the southeastern United States, has issued an arrest warrant for 95-year-old former Cuban leader Raul Castro .

The move comes as US authorities step up pressure on the government in Havana.

State Attorney General James Uthmeier said on Monday that the warrant was based on criminal charges over Castro’s alleged role in ordering two unarmed aircraft to be shot down in 1996 .

The aircraft were affiliated with Brothers to the Rescue, a Florida-based group that helps Cubans fleeing the country. Four people were killed in the attack.

Castro faces state-level charges of conspiracy to commit first-degree murder in Florida.

“Raul Castro ordered the murder of four Floridians in cold blood, and Florida will never stop pursuing accountability for that communist conspiracy,” Uthmeier wrote in a news release.

He said the arrest warrant was necessary accountability for the lives lost. “Thirty years later, we are still fighting for justice for Carlos Costa, Pablo Morales, Mario de la Pena, and Armando Alejandre Jr.”

The decision to shoot down the two small twin-engine planes has been the subject of renewed controversy over the last year, as Republican President Donald Trump seeks to oust Cuba’s communist leaders.

The attack took place on February 24, 1996. US authorities say the planes were flying over international waters and received no warning before they were shot down.

Cuban officials, meanwhile, have argued that previous Brothers to the Rescue flights had breached the country’s airspace, despite warnings to stay away.

Castro, now 95 years old, was Cuba’s defence minister at the time of the attack. A key figure in the Communist Party of Cuba, he later became president of the island in 2008, replacing his brother, the late revolutionary leader Fidel Castro.

Though he retired from the presidency in 2018, Raul Castro and his family remain powerful figures in Cuba’s government.

Since the start of the year, the Trump administration has signalled it would like to see regime change in Cuba.

To trigger such change, the administration has tightened US restrictions on the island, including by imposing a de facto energy blockade in January.

By threatening steep tariffs against any country that supplies Cuba with oil, the US has effectively barred fuel exports to the country, according to experts.

That, in turn, has caused deteriorating conditions on the island and strained the country’s already meagre power system, which relies heavily on fossil fuels. Only 40 percent of Cuba’s oil is produced domestically.

Additional sanctions have been placed on Cuba’s economy, limiting its state-run industries.

But in May, the Trump administration unveiled a superseding indictment also targeting Raul Castro for the 1996 plane downings.

It charges Castro with federal crimes including conspiracy to kill US nationals, destroying aircraft and four counts of murder.

The Trump administration issued a statement in support of Florida’s actions against Castro on Monday.

“We’re committed to pursuing every lawful, prosecutable avenue to bring accountability, including parallel federal and state prosecutions,” US Attorney Jason Reding Quinones said.

“Our historic federal indictment laid the groundwork, and James [Uthmeier] and his team have now taken the important step of bringing charges under Florida law.”

Trump has previously used indictments to justify military operations targeting government leaders that are at odds with the US, including former Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro .

articles.title: US Federal authorities responding to shooting at mosque in Columbus, Ohio
articles.summary: This is a breaking news story.
articles.body:
United States federal authorities are responding to a shooting at a mosque in Columbus, Ohio, according to the local office of the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco and Firearms and Explosives.

The agency said its agents were responding to the shooting. It posted the alert at 3:28pm local (19:28GMT).

“ATF Columbus Field Division Special Agents are responding to a reported shooting incident at a mosque in the 2200 block of Albert Ave. in Columbus, OH,” it said.

“Additional information will be shared as it becomes available.”

Further details were not immediately available.
